system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Seller Draft Review Against Buyer Playbook

**Bottom line:** The Seller's package departs from our playbook on almost every material point. It would cap general recovery at about AUD 4.8m, let title and capacity claims be capped and time-barred like general warranties, shield the Seller behind a broad buyer-knowledge bar and data-room deemed disclosure, and leave Bluefen, Riverlark and the employee bonuses unresolved at Completion. We should not accept any of it as a base for mark-up.

## 1. Departures from the playbook

| Issue | Seller draft | Our playbook | Pushback |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6m start. 20% is a fallback that needs Amelia Frost's written authority, which has not been given | Counter at 25% / AUD 6m. Do not signal 20% |
| De minimis (12.2) | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | Reject |
| Basket (12.2) | AUD 250,000, excess-only recovery (deductible) | AUD 50,000, first-dollar once exceeded | Reject. Seller liable from first dollar |
| General claims period (12.3/13) | 18 months | 24 months (18 needs Frost approval) | Counter at 24 months |
| Limitation applies to "all Claims" unless stated otherwise (12.3/13) | Blanket override | Categories kept separate; no hidden general-regime override | Reject. Cut the default-to-general wording |
| Fundamental/Title (12.x) | Same caps and time limits as general warranties | 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar | Reject outright |
| Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance (9.3/12.8/20.5) | Apply to "all Claims of any nature" | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance | Add express carve-out. Silence is not enough |
| Disclosure (Sch 7; DL 1.1, 1.2) | Whole data room, Accounts, statutory registers and public searches | Specific fair disclosure only; reject data-room and public-register deemed disclosure | Reject. Delete the "without limiting" language |
| Buyer knowledge (8.3) | Bars claims for anything Buyer or advisers knew or could find in data room or public records | Delete blanket exclusion. Any qualifier needs named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities | Reject |
| Bluefen (3, 6.3) | Reasonable endeavours; satisfied on delivery of consent | Effective consent and evidence that conditions are met before Completion; reasonable endeavours is insufficient | Make it a Completion condition with evidence. DL 2 confirms no final consent |
| Riverlark (2, 7) | ~AUD 3.2m released after Completion | Current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security release. Post-Completion release only with irrevocable undertaking and Frost approval | Require payout letter and direct repayment in funds flow |
| Employee bonuses (DD-005, funds flow) | AUD 420k "a matter for the Seller", not in funds flow | Specific line item or Seller-funded; not silently excluded | Add a specific, Seller-funded line item covering triggered on-costs |
| Ironquay IP (11.1) | Narrow indemnity limited to SOW3 payment; "adequate" | Broaden indemnity; preserve SOW3 cure | Reject "adequate". Broaden the indemnity. Do not take a view on the AUD 180k either way |
| Export/privacy incident (4.6, Sch 6; DD-006) | "Preliminary", "not expected to be material" | Preserve logs, investigate, require updates. Assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand | Require preservation, investigation and updates. Do not accept the materiality conclusion |
| Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k) | "Ordinary-course operating costs" | Assess. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction | Accept assessment only. Reject the characterisation as settled |
| Tax / IP | "Settled under the general regime" | Open. Assume no unlimited liability and no resolution | Reject. Keep these as separate categories and open |
| Title (DD-012) | Share register evidences 100% title | DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof | Require independent title, encumbrance and authority evidence |

## 2. Reasoning on the material issues

**Caps and thresholds.** The combined effect is significant. A 20% cap, a AUD 250k excess-only basket and a 25k de minimis mean that a buyer with AUD 300k of valid claims would recover only AUD 50k, and small claims would not count at all. Our 50k first-dollar basket and 5k de minimis are the minimum we can justify.

**Title and fundamental warranties.** This is the most serious point. Putting capacity and title under general caps and time limits would expose us to losing a title claim after 18 months or to a cap below the price. Title is the core of what we are buying. The 100% cap and six-year period are non-negotiable.

**Fraud carve-out.** The seller's text does not carve out fraud from the limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions. Without an express carve-out, a deliberate concealment could be argued to be barred. This must be fixed in the mark-up, and no one can waive it.

**Disclosure and buyer knowledge together.** Deemed disclosure of the whole data room, plus a buyer-knowledge bar covering anything "discoverable", would neutralise most warranty claims. Buyers almost always have some knowledge of data-room content. Our position is specific disclosure only and no knowledge bar that reaches title, capacity or fraud.

**Completion-critical consents and payouts.** Bluefen (about AUD 3.6m, ~30% of FY26 revenue) and Riverlark (about AUD 3.2m) both go to whether the business can be transferred and the security released. The seller's post-Completion approach would leave us exposed to a lender claim over the company and a material customer walking away. The Disclosure Letter confirms neither is satisfied now.

**Funds flow.** The bonuses are a seller obligation as the seller describes them, yet they are absent from the funds flow. Without a line item, the cost falls on the company after Completion. On-costs (payroll tax, superannuation) are not yet quantified and must be included.

**Ironquay, incident and supplier items.** These are diligence items that the seller has characterised favourably. Our role is to preserve our rights (broader indemnity, log preservation, investigation updates, assessment of the Sandbar renewals) without accepting the seller's conclusions in either direction.

**Other items not in the playbook.** The office lease (DD-007) notification and the Mossvale (DD-009) assignment restriction both need a confirmed answer on whether consent is required. We should not assume either way.

**Disclosure date.** The Disclosure Letter speaks as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, and today is 6 November 2026. We should require a bring-down disclosure at signing and Completion.

## 3. Summary of recommendations

1. **Reject the Seller's package as a base.** Mark up from our playbook: 25% / AUD 6m cap, AUD 5k de minimis, AUD 50k first-dollar basket, 24-month general period.
2. **Separate the regimes.** Title, capacity and fundamental warranties: 100% cap, six years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar. Delete the "all Claims" default.
3. **Add an express fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate-misconduct carve-out** from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance.
4. **Strike** the whole-data-room, statutory-register and public-search disclosure, and the blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion. Require specific fair disclosure.
5. **Make Bluefen a Completion condition:** effective consent plus evidence that the 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
6. **Riverlark:** payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security release. No post-Completion release without an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
7. **Funds flow:** add a specific line item for the AUD 420k bonuses plus triggered on-costs, Seller-funded.
8. **Ironquay:** broaden the 11.1 indemnity and preserve the SOW3 cure.
9. **Incident (DD-006):** require log preservation, investigation and regular updates. Do not accept the materiality conclusion. Consider a specific indemnity as a negotiating option, subject to principal sign-off.
10. **Sandbar renewals:** require assessment of whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable or accrued. No automatic debt treatment or price deduction.
11. **Tax and IP:** reject "settled". Keep as open, separate categories.
12. **Title:** require independent title, encumbrance and authority evidence (for example, registry extracts and PPSR searches), not DD-012 alone.
13. **Other:** confirm the landlord consent position (DD-007) and the Mossvale position (DD-009). Require a bring-down disclosure.
14. **Authority:** do not offer the 20% cap or 18-month period in the mark-up. Neither is authorised.

This is a commercial and legal analysis to support your deal team. Before the mark-up goes to the Seller, it should be checked by NSW-qualified transaction counsel, particularly the carve-out wording, the disclosure drafting and the Bluefen and Riverlark conditions.
=== END ADVICE ===
